title: systemTest actor/credential path: provisioning is never invoked, so the generated-actor path never resolves — and exactly one site (the SYSTEM_ADMIN persona) can never use it
description:
**KS-966 item 4 was stood down on measurement.** It was scoped as *"route the 12 systemTest sites through the existing generated-actor path"*. **That path never runs**, and for one site it could not work even if it did. This is the one logical path — the systemTest actor/credential story — with its items inside it, per Kam's 2026-09-07 13:23 rule.

## Searched before filing (958 issues, including archived)

| searched | hits |
| -- | -- |
| SYMBOL `getGeneratedActor` | KS-966 only (this ticket's parent) |
| SYMBOL `ADMIN_ACTOR_KEY` | KS-966 only |
| SYMBOL `provision-actors` | KS-966 only |
| PATH `systemTest/fixtures/generated` | **none** |
| SYMBOL `TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD` | KS-967 only (as a guarded key name, different subject) |
| STRING `actor manifest` / `actors.json` | **none** |

**No existing ticket covers this.** Four sessions worked this repo today, so the check was worth making.

---

## ITEM 1 — Wire actor provisioning into a pre-suite step

`getGeneratedActor()` reads `systemTest/fixtures/generated/actors.json` (`playwright/config/actorManifest.ts:45`) and returns `undefined` when absent. Measured on `origin/develop`:

* **0** files tracked under `systemTest/fixtures/generated`; the manifest is **absent** on a fresh tree.
* Written **only** by `systemTest/fixtures/provision-actors.ts`.
* **Nothing automated invokes it**: no npm script · no `.github` workflow · no shell runner · **not** `playwright/global-setup.ts` (imports only `getApiBaseUrl`) · **not** `auth/auth.setup.ts` (imports `getTestAdminEmail`/`getTestAdminPassword` and logs in with them). Its only references are its own docstring showing manual invocation.
* **CONTROL:** the same `git grep` over the same paths finds `"test:unit"` in `playwright/package.json`. The instrument fires, so the zeros are real zeros.

**So the fallbacks are the live path, not redundancy.** This item is a pre-suite hook (a Playwright setup-project dependency, or the slot runner) **with its own test** — not a tail-end edit.

## ITEM 2 — The SYSTEM_ADMIN split. **M = 1**, and here it is

Of the 12 occurrences, **8 are documentary** (comments, docstrings, `@example` blocks) and belong to KS-965, not here. **Four are executable credential sources**, and three of them are satisfied by `orgAdmin`:

| site | drives | verdict |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `schemathesis/tests/conftest.py:83` | `resolve_credentials("orgAdmin", …)` | **already keyed to** `orgAdmin`, with env override + fallback |
| `schemathesis/scripts/setup_api_key.py:53` | `POST /api/admin/api-keys`, gated `requireRole('SYSTEM_ADMIN','ORG_ADMIN')` | **ORG_ADMIN is admitted** by the route |
| `schemathesis/tests/test_authentication.py:26` | `POST /auth/login` only (success / invalid / missing-field) | **login requires no role at all** |
| `schemathesis/config/fixtures.py:82` | `Persona(key="super_admin", role="SYSTEM_ADMIN", …)` — *"Cross-tenant reads via X-Tenant-Override"* | **🔴 genuinely requires SYSTEM_ADMIN** |

**So exactly ONE site cannot be served by the generated-actor path** — and it cannot be served by design, not by omission. The manifest module says so in its own words:

> *"*`orgAdmin` *stands in for* `admin`*: SYSTEM_ADMIN is deliberately not grantable through the API, so it can never be generated."*

**That single site is the whole decision.** Either its cross-tenant persona keeps a seeded SYSTEM_ADMIN credential supplied by environment, or the suite loses cross-tenant coverage. **Nothing else in the 12 needs a ruling.**

## ITEM 3 — `TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD` is documented, but documented WRONG

The concern raised was that it might be undocumented. **It is named** — `playwright/README.md:27` and `:152`, `playwright/docs/setup_guide.md:89` and `:238`. **The defect is sharper than absence:**

* `playwright/.env.example:27` has it **commented out**, so `cp .env.example .env` supplies nothing.
* `playwright/docs/setup_guide.md:89` documents its **default as the retired literal** — a value that no longer works, because #888 removed the seeder's published default *and* the `getTestAdminPassword()` fallback.

**So a runner who follows the documentation sets a password that cannot authenticate**, and with GitHub Actions retired (20 of 20 runs `startup_failure`, measured 2026-09-07) nothing fails loudly to tell them. **This is an operational precondition #888 introduced without updating its documentation.** The security change was right; this is its unpaid half.

Both of those lines also carry the retired literal and are in KS-965's documentary census — **fix them here, since here is where their wrongness is load-bearing.**

## ITEM 4 — Only then, the 12 sites

Blocked on items 1–3. Doing it first inverts the F3 error corrected on KS-968 today: removing the harmless thing and leaving the one that detonates.

---

*Filed by s146 from the KS-966 item-4 measurement. Items 3 and 4 of KS-966 are closed by comment against this ticket. The 12/8/4/1 counts are mine and were re-derived after I found my first pass had omitted* `.py` *from its extension list — which had hidden six of the eight executable files.*

State corrected: In Review to In Progress. Item 1 is delivered; the rest of the actor/credential path is open.

Done: PR 892 (item 1, f54b2dce1; merged 512480ef1) runs actor provisioning as a pre-suite step and makes the fallback loud. PR 989 (a9ce2cff1, from KS-973) is also merged. Both are ancestors of the kintsugi deploy b1fb543640e7. A 2026-10-09 comment on this ticket measured provisioning invoked before every suite run (8 runs, 4 suites).

Left: the ticket's 2026-09-13 comment keeps open what supplies BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD to a local or CI test stack ("a DESIGN answer, not a value"). The SYSTEM_ADMIN persona still cannot use the generated-actor path (comments of 2026-09-14 and 2026-09-28). No deployed commit subject names item 2, 3 or 4 of this ticket as delivered.

For context: these results were measured on the KS-1455 branch (`feature/ks-1455-bump-systemtest-schemathesis-pin-4294-4300-or-later-release`, PR https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1438), which is going to be merged today.

**A data point from the KS-1455 runs (2026-10-09, slot 4, `bf9568582`)**, offered in case it helps the review.

Actor provisioning **was invoked** before every suite run. Each run logged `[pre-suite:<suite>] PROVISIONED — 5 generated actor(s) from seed "local"` and wrote `fixtures/generated/actors-slot4.json`:
* Schemathesis `pr` and `full` ×2
* Akto `pre-merge`
* Playwright
* k6 `smoke`, `load` and `soak`

That's 8 runs across 4 suites. The five actors were owner, issuer, approver, verifier and orgAdmin, with roles assigned by the bootstrap admin.

What this does **not** show: anything about the SYSTEM_ADMIN persona site this ticket names. No run here exercised that path in a way I could observe, so that half is still open.

Evidence: https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1438

A small update from KS-1353, in case it's useful. I'm not claiming anything on this ticket; the wider actor-path gap is still yours.

One consequence of the SYSTEM_ADMIN persona not being able to use the generated-actor path turned out to be quite loud. Under `run-in-slot.sh` the manifest exists, so `TEST_CREDENTIALS["admin"]` resolved to the `orgAdmin` stand-in (`ks256-orgadmin-local@secuura-test.invalid`, **ORG_ADMIN**). Five live tests that needed a real super-admin then reported **KS-467 / KS-513 cross-tenant disclosure**. The platform was scoping and refusing that ORG_ADMIN exactly as it should, so they were false alarms, and while the persona was wrong they weren't exercising isolation at all.

What changed in systemTest (commit `3394ae664`, not yet pushed): those tests now resolve a genuine platform admin through `tests/support/platform_admin.py`. That means `TEST_ADMIN_*` first, then the bootstrap SYSTEM_ADMIN via `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, never the stand-in. The role is also verified from the issued token, so a wrong persona now fails as a named precondition rather than as a security finding. Same modules, same invocation: 5 failed / 2 errors → 29 passed. With a real super-admin, KS-467 scoping and KS-513 isolation both hold.

`TEST_CREDENTIALS["admin"]` itself is unchanged, and so is anything else that relies on the stand-in. Thank you. Nothing needed from you on this.

**Live instance of the SYSTEM_ADMIN-persona seam, 2026-09-14 (slot 4, KS-1167 run).** Schemathesis's `super_admin` persona is hardcoded to the seed `admin@secuura.com / admin123` (`config/fixtures.py:92-95`) and cannot take a provisioned actor. I had seeded slot 4 with a non-default `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD`; the k6, Playwright and Akto suites were fine (they authenticate as provisioned actors via `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD`), but `run.py pr` 401'd on every persona login until the brute-force limiter engaged — **325 errors, all `login for persona=super_admin is rate-limited`**, sweep reported FAILED, report/baseline gate skipped (KS-752). Remedy was to reseed with the published value and `--fresh-db`. So today the only working configuration for Schemathesis is the credential KS-966 is retiring — this persona site is the blocker for both tickets.

Related, same session: four suites back-to-back on one slot inside one 15-minute window exhaust that slot's per-IP login window (`RateLimit-Policy: 100;w=900`) regardless of `LOCAL_LOGIN_LIMITER_DISABLED` — 891 rate-limited errors on slot 2; clean after a 15-minute gap. The KS-1167 pre-suite banner now names the limiter rather than the password when this happens.

**Held open — a residue by this ticket's own words; not moved by the 2026-09-14 class-h pass** (card secuura-fourteen-merged-own-pr-tickets-never-moved, close-by-residue; re-verified at source by s218).
- Residue (comment 2c2b7e02, 2026-09-10): "The open question in e1358ef7 is unchanged: what supplies BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD to a local or CI test stack now that the published default is retired? Setting a value to make the suite pass is still ruled out"; comment 39869627 (2026-09-08): the answer "must be a DESIGN answer, not a value." KS-973 (Todo) carries 0 hits for BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD — the design question is not there; KS-966 (In Progress, unassigned) is the sibling retire ticket.
- Develop probe (read 2026-09-14 at `8861e62161466c40f08d2b10a30edeb203123993`): `systemTest/CLAUDE.md:1203-1206` (blob `9f54bf7b4923`) still instructs "Set BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD on EVERY suite run, including Schemathesis" — the supply is a manual export, which is the open design question, not its answer. 14 files at develop name the variable; none decides where a local or CI stack gets it.
- PR #892 merged 2026-09-07T23:31:43Z as `512480ef107349a61b3da89eb3af4e8a31e65d84` (item 1: provisioning as a pre-suite step). Lane family: systemTest (Peter's authority by the ticket's own words); a design ruling first (Wednesday's or Kam's), then the change.
- Stays open; not moved by the 2026-09-14 class-h pass. No state write, nothing deployed, no environment touched.

**Evidence added here, not a new ticket.** Wednesday commissioned a ticket for "the KS-969 / KS-966 composition seam". I searched the board before filing it, and **it is already recorded on this ticket** in comment `e1358ef7` (2026-09-08, *"The defect is step 5, and it is narrow"*). So this adds s171's CI measurement to it rather than opening a second ticket.

**Search, so the absence is checkable:**
- Exact `getTestAdminPassword`: KS-969 only.
- `correctly-roled`, `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `provision-actors.ts`: noisy. I opened KS-973, KS-967, KS-977 and KS-915, and none carries this.
- Control `KS-969`: 1 hit.

## What CI adds to the 2026-09-08 local reading
From s171's review of the PR #896 run logs, 2026-09-10:
- The empty-password login inside `auth.setup` returns **HTTP 400, not 401**. Validation rejects it before authentication runs, so the error a reader sees is one step further from its cause than the 401 above.
- The Playwright step is red having run **0 of 11** tests: `1 failed / 11 did not run`.
- On `develop` `2d864ae92`, `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` is set in **0** workflow files. Control: `API_BASE_URL` appears in 4.

## Where it sits on `develop` now (re-read at `2d864ae92`)
- `systemTest/fixtures/pre-suite.ts:114`: the DEGRADED banner still promises *"the suite keeps its correctly-roled SEEDED accounts"*.
- `systemTest/fixtures/pre-suite.ts:110`: `exitCode: required ? 1 : 0`. DEGRADED exits **0** unless `SYSTEMTEST_REQUIRE_PROVISIONED` is set, so the run carries on into the failure.
- `systemTest/fixtures/provision-actors.ts:110`: `password: process.env.BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD ?? ''`. On #896's head the same line is `:155`.
- `systemTest/playwright/config/environment.ts:179`: `getTestAdminPassword()`, whose terminal fallback is `''` (KS-966 site 8).

The open question in `e1358ef7` is unchanged: what supplies `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` to a local or CI test stack now that the published default is retired? Setting a value to make the suite pass is still ruled out. This comment records evidence only and fixes nothing, because `systemTest/` is Peter's authority. The sibling finding, that the Playwright env guard in #896 cannot see this variable, is filed separately and linked here.

## Evidence for THIS ticket's open design question — from the KS-1013 gate (F-6)

The QA gate measured something on the local stack that bears directly on the `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` question this ticket holds:

**The local SYSTEM_ADMIN credential is a historical artefact, not a reproducible seed.**

* `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS` is **SET BUT EMPTY**
* `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` is **unset**
* so the seeder **short-circuits** — and **a COLD START would have no usable admin at all**

Login works today only because the row survives from an earlier run. **Nobody has provisioned that credential; it is left over.**

**Why it belongs here rather than as its own ticket:** this ticket's open question is *what SHOULD supply an admin credential in a local test stack now the published default is retired*. ⛔ It was ruled that the answer must be a DESIGN answer, not a value — setting `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` to unblock a suite is how a retired default comes back.

**F-6 is evidence that the question is not hypothetical.** The current answer is "an artefact of an earlier run", which survives exactly until someone runs a clean stack. Any future gate that depends on that persona is depending on a row nobody can recreate.

**Not established:** whether a cold start has actually been attempted — the gate inferred the short-circuit from the env vars and the seeder's code path, and did not restart anything.

*Measured by the QA gate during the KS-1013 / PR #910 tier-1 pass, 2026-09-09. Relayed via Wednesday; the env-var readings are the gate's.*

## ⚠ PREMISE CORRECTION — provisioning IS invoked; it runs and correctly REFUSES

**BLUF: the title is false as measured. `provisioning is never invoked` — it was invoked six times tonight, on the same stack, with the same result each time.** A reader who takes the title at face value will go looking for a provisioner that does not run and find one that does. **The failure is real and still reproduces; only the mechanism in the title is wrong.**

Measured s153, 2026-09-08, against images rebuilt at develop `5ffaaf396` — four schemathesis `pr` runs, one k6 smoke, one Playwright run. Six invocations, identical output.

## What actually happens — the suite prints its own diagnosis

    [provision-actors] seed "local" -> 5 actors against http://localhost:6882
    [provision-actors] 4 actor(s) hold a role other than the one requested
        (issuer, approver, verifier, orgAdmin). MANIFEST NOT PUBLISHED —
        suites keep their seeded accounts. Rejected copy: fixtures/generated/actors.rejected.json
    [pre-suite:playwright] DEGRADED — 4 actor(s) did not get the role they were provisioned for.
    [pre-suite:playwright] This is almost always BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD being unset:
        no self-service path can grant a role, so every actor lands as OWNER.

The chain, end to end:

1. **`BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` is unset.** The KS-949 / KS-964 / KS-966 rotation retired the published SYSTEM_ADMIN default and nothing supplies a replacement in a local test stack.
2. No self-service path can grant a role, so **all five actors land as `OWNER`** (`via: existing`).
3. Four drift from the role requested, so the provisioner **refuses to publish**, writes `fixtures/generated/actors.rejected.json`, **and moves any previously published `actors.json` aside**.
4. Playwright reads `fixtures/generated/actors.json`. It is absent **by design**.
5. `getGeneratedActor(ADMIN_ACTOR_KEY)?.password ?? ''` → **empty string**.
6. `auth.setup` posts an empty password → 401 → the suite's dependency edge suppresses everything downstream.

## 🟢 Steps 1–3 are the guard WORKING — do not "fix" them

The refusal is correct, and the reason it lives in the filesystem rather than in a reader is written into its own comment: `schemathesis/tests/actor_manifest.py` parses the JSON directly, so a TypeScript-side staleness check would never have covered it, and any consumer that forgot one would silently keep the old behaviour. It also moves a superseded manifest aside rather than deleting it, because **a non-write is not a removal** — an earlier pass's `actors.json` would otherwise still be the file every consumer reads.

## The defect is step 5, and it is narrow

The refusal promises *"suites keep their correctly-roled SEEDED accounts"*. **Every other consumer honours that. Playwright's admin path does not** — it falls back to `''` rather than to a seeded account, so a **DEGRADED** run becomes a **FAILED** one.

⚠ **The `?? ''` is deliberate and its intent is right.** Its own comment names it *"KS-966 site 8"*: an empty string is substituted so that a run with no generated actor **fails as an empty credential rather than authenticating on a value published in this repository**. **The intent is correct; the consequence is that the one suite reading that path cannot fall back at all.** This should not read as anyone's mistake.

## The blast radius, in the order that does not mislead

> **Coverage 0 of 12 — of which 1 failed and 11 did not run.**

`auth-setup` is a dependency, so its failure suppresses the whole `api` project. **Reported as "1 failed" out of a twelve-test suite it reads as 92% green, and the true figure is nothing at all.** The count is 1; the coverage is zero. Worth stating in that order for any suite with a dependency edge.

## 🔴 OPEN QUESTION — and `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` must NOT just be set

The one-line unblock looks like supplying `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD`. **It was deliberately not tried, and Wednesday has ruled explicitly that it must not be** (2026-09-08): setting a credential in order to make a suite pass is the anti-pattern, and this one sits on the very rotation surface whose purpose was retiring a published default. **A value that unblocks a test is exactly how a retired default comes back.**

> **The question this ticket needs answered: what is supposed to supply `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` in a local test stack now that the published default is retired?**

That is a design answer, not a value.

## Suggested retitle

*"systemTest actor provisioning is refused (all actors land as OWNER with BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD unset) — and Playwright's admin path falls back to an empty credential instead of a seeded account"*

## Also measured, unchanged from s152

`quality:static` **4 errors** (same file, same lines — 3 of 4 `--fix`-able) · `test:unit` **48/48** · `test:e2e` **1 failed / 11 did not run**. Byte-for-byte the same as the pre-rebuild run, so **this High has not quietly fixed itself.**

*No fix attempted. Nothing changed. Reported only.*

## LIVE REPRODUCTION — this ticket was filed from a static read; here it is executing

Ran the Playwright platform suite against a **fully-up local stack** (33/33 services, gateway healthy)
on 2026-09-08. **The defect this ticket describes is what breaks the suite.**

    test:e2e   →   1 FAILED, 11 DID NOT RUN
    auth-setup › authenticate once and persist session
    POST /api/auth/login  --data '{ "email": "admin@secuura.com", "password": "" }'

### The chain, traced end to end

1. `auth/auth.setup.ts:24` builds its payload from `getTestAdminEmail()` / `getTestAdminPassword()`.
2. `config/environment.ts:179` `getTestAdminPassword()` resolves **`TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD`** first.
3. The suite's `.env` carries **six** keys and `TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD` is **not one of them** — it has
   `TEST_USER_PASSWORD` (a different key). Measured by name and length only, never values:
   `API_TOKEN`, `TEST_USER_EMAIL`, `TEST_USER_PASSWORD`, `HEADLESS`, `TIMEOUT`, `SCREENSHOT_ON_FAILURE`.
4. So it falls through to the generated-actor path — **which this ticket establishes is never
   invoked** — and reaches the terminal fallback.
5. It returns **`''`**. The function's own docblock says so in terms:
   *`getTestAdminPassword(); // '' unless an actor was provisioned`*.
6. Login posts an empty password and fails.

### Why the blast radius is the part worth recording

**`1 failed / 11 did not run`.** The eleven are the `api` project, which declares `auth-setup` as a
dependency — so when setup fails, **none of them execute**. The suite's headline reads as one failure;
what actually happened is that **zero of twelve tests exercised the system**.

That matters beyond this ticket: the four platform suites are the merge gate, and this one can report
a single red while asserting nothing at all about the platform. It is the same shape as KS-1010 — a
suite going green (or nearly-green) by not running.

### Attribution

Not a platform defect: the stack was healthy, and preflight legs 3 and 4 passed **321/321** and
**341/341** probed against the same gateway in the same session. The failure is entirely the harness's
credential-resolution chain, which is this ticket.

*Added by s152 — reproduced, not inferred. Nothing changed; no `.env` was edited and no credential was
written.*

## #892 MERGED — round 5 closes it. `develop` `4f337be83` → **`512480ef107349a61b3da89eb3af4e8a31e65d84`**

Gate verdict: **GO with findings — no Blocker, no Major.** Both round-4 Majors closed and independently red-proofed by the gate.

**Merge receipt, verified from the object and not from the API response:**

```
predicted tree oid (BEFORE)  3f7d2a6d16b62783ce031ffc90e61e82ff9c361c
actual    tree oid (AFTER)   3f7d2a6d16b62783ce031ffc90e61e82ff9c361c   ✓
parents, re-derived from the commit object:
    4f337be838cfeea56b77628ddfe19619a1884186   (develop)
    d2aa11fd10ccaed1da6ebbb36a18c92fc2fdf363   (#892)
head read back from origin, not from the merge response: 512480ef1
```

Negative controls, all 0 in the predicted tree: #793's `audit-baseline.json`, #720's `BACKLOG.md`, #721's `CLAUDE.md`, **and any `Blockchain/Dev/` path**. 12 files changed, all under `systemTest/`.

### What round 5 closed

**F-2 — the suite quarantined the developer's live manifest.** Reproduced first: a sentinel `actors.json` was renamed away by a run reporting `29 passed, 0 failed`, rc 0. Fixed with the stash/restore + `trap … EXIT` from `quarantine_call_sites.test.sh`. **The gate's independent red-proof met the binding condition verbatim** — trap removed, manifest destroyed, trailer still `25 passed, 0 FAILED`. The suite's report is provably blind to it, which is why no added cell could have closed it.

**F-1 — `runPreSuite` could throw against its own `:90` docstring.** The in-catch `quarantineManifest()` call is wrapped, and the failure is **reported rather than swallowed** — swallowing is worse, because a surviving stale manifest outranks the seeded accounts in every consumer. **The gate went further than my red-proof:** it asserted the contract on the *function* rather than the CLI exit code — CONTRACT HELD at head, CONTRACT BROKEN at parent, same instrument. TOCTOU reproduced **11/12 at parent, 0/12 at head**, with all 24 processes accounted for and the race entered 10 times and handled 10 times — so the zero is not vacuous.

### The cell count: 29, 25 and 24 are all correct

The brief said 24, I measured **29**, the gate measured **25**. The gate explained the delta: it gates off the live PROVISIONED arm (4 cells) because that arm creates accounts on `:6882`. **25 + 4 = 29.** Only the configuration differs.

### State deliberately NOT changed

Wednesday reserved the `Tested Not Deployed` question for this work. **I have not moved this ticket** — the state choice *is* that question, and it is hers. Nothing has been deployed; the demo remains on `400517aaf` and this round does not change that.

### Follow-ups filed, none blocking

- **KS-992** — both quarantine guards `rm -rf` a directory they may have failed to snapshot (class note, names both files, carries the gate's honest limit: mechanism proven, realistic trigger not).
- **KS-993** — nothing type-checks `systemTest/fixtures/`, so this round's own TypeScript was checked by no compiler.
- **[KS-973](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-973)** — a second unguarded `quarantineManifest` at `provision-actors.ts:178` (untested, though structurally safe), and the `invokedDirectly` symlink curio.
- **[KS-989](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-989)** — the gate's "THERE IS CI" finding, reconciled three ways after I re-derived it: configured **yes**, executing in Actions **no**, executing locally **no** (preflight leg 12 is `--check-unreached`, a reachability assertion, not an execution).

## ITEM 2 — partition RE-DERIVED at `develop` `6c60cc09b`. The ticket was right; a mail was wrong; and the real defect is that the PREDICATE was never written down.

## BLUF
**8 documentary · 4 executable · M = 1. This item's existing text is CORRECT and stands.** The
conflicting version — *"12 occurrences across 8 EXECUTABLE files"* — is **wrong**: it inverted the
label. It is 8 **documentary**, and they are occurrences, not files.
**But re-deriving it took four candidate predicates, because "the 12" was never anchored to one.**
That is the finding, and the predicate is now recorded below so nobody re-derives it again.

## THE PREDICATE — the thing that was missing
> Occurrences of the literal `admin123` in **`systemTest/schemathesis/`** plus
> **`systemTest/fixtures/actors.ts`** (the generator's own header, which names the schemathesis and
> playwright credentials).

`git grep -an "admin123" <sha> -- systemTest/schemathesis systemTest/fixtures/actors.ts` → **exactly 12**.

**Predicates that do NOT give 12**, recorded so the number is never re-fitted to a different scope:
`admin123` in all of `systemTest/` = **23** · `admin@secuura.com` in `systemTest/` = **41** ·
`SYSTEM_ADMIN` in `systemTest/` = **74** · `SYSTEM_ADMIN` in `systemTest/schemathesis/` = **34** ·
`admin123` in `systemTest/schemathesis/` alone = **10**.

## THE 12, CLASSIFIED BY READING EACH ONE
**EXECUTABLE — 4** (a live path reads the value):
`config/fixtures.py:82` `password="admin123"` · `scripts/setup_api_key.py:53`
`DEFAULT_ADMIN_PASSWORD = "admin123"` · `tests/conftest.py:83` (the `resolve_credentials` fallback) ·
`tests/test_authentication.py:26` `TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD: str = "admin123"`.

**DOCUMENTARY — 8** (a human reads it): `fixtures/actors.ts:11` and `:12` (header comment) ·
